ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A person rides a bicycle along a straight path at a speed of $v$ for two-thirds of the distance, then rides the remaining one-third of the distance at a speed of $5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

1. If the average speed throughout the journey is $3\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, then what is $v$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A person rides a bicycle along a straight path at a speed of $v$ for two-thirds of the distance, then rides the remaining one-third of the distance at a speed of $5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. If the average speed throughout the journey is $3\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, then what is $v$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let the total distance be D. The first segment is two-thirds of the distance, so its length is 2D/3 and the time taken is (2D/3)/v = 2D/(3v). The second segment is one-third of the distance, so its length is D/3 and the time taken at 5 m/s is (D/3)/5 = D/15. Therefore the total time is 2D/(3v) + D/15. The average speed is total distance divided by total time, so D / [2D/(3v) + D/15] = 3. Canceling D gives 1 / [2/(3v) + 1/15] = 3, so 2/(3v) + 1/15 = 1/3. Then 2/(3v) = 1/3 - 1/15 = 4/15. Solving 2/(3v) = 4/15 gives 30 = 12v, hence v = 2.5 m/s.
